result.headline: Throttle commanded to zero at 103.3 s; the aircraft lost attitude control about 10 s later and descended.
result.explanation: Propulsion loop (throttle and ch[2]) went to zero and stayed there with no recorded mode or failsafe event. Attitude control and altitude then degraded, which fits loss of thrust. Who or what cut the throttle is not in the data.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT propulsion.throttle was varying, then held 0 from t=103.268 s to the end of the recording (20.916 s, 54 samples)
evidence.shows: Throttle dropped from a median of 52 to 0 and never came back. compare at 103.268 flags it as frozen (z 8.7), and no event or mode change explains it.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT actuator.output[ch[2]] was varying, then held 1100 from t=104.109 s to the end of the recording (20.136 s, 61 samples)
evidence.shows: The ch[2] output followed the throttle to its minimum (correlation 0.992 at lag 0.677 s), so the output stage obeyed the command.

evidence.quote: ROLE actuator.output[ch[2]] follows propulsion.throttle (correlation 0.969 over the recording): it serves that loop
evidence.shows: ch[2] is the propulsion channel. It is the one that froze while the other channels kept moving.

evidence.quote: SHIFT vehicle.altitude[relative] changed level for good at t=114.148 s: median 50.145 before, 33.326 after m
evidence.shows: Altitude fell from about 50 m to 16.701 m by the end, after the throttle cut.

evidence.quote: ANOMALY a9 t=113.559 s: vehicle.attitude[yaw] did not follow control.attitude_setpoint[yaw] (peak |error| 30.292)
evidence.shows: Attitude tracking broke down about 10 s after the throttle cut. Typical error rose by ratios of 3.54 to 4.63 at 113.6 s.

checked.check: Sequence of what left baseline first, 100 to 118 s
checked.result: Roll and yaw setpoints left baseline first (100.075 s), then roll attitude, ch[2] (100.997 s), throttle (101.42 s) and pitch setpoint. Roll attitude reached 43.982 deg shortly before the throttle cut. This shows a disturbance before the cut, not what caused it.
Throttle level change z 1.7 and tracking unchanged or better. Not a fault onset.
Throttle median 52 to 0 (frozen), ch[2] 1512 to 1100, velocity[y] 16.385 to -0.01 m/s, velocity[x] -2.37 to -15.91 m/s. Attitude tracking error stayed small (2.558 pitch, 2.569 roll).
Tracking error rose in roll, yaw and pitch (ratio 4.63, 4.35, 3.54). ch[1], ch[3], ch[4] and ch[5] shifted while ch[2] was unchanged at 1100.
checked.about: Loss of control as an effect of the propulsion loss

checked.check: relation throttle to ch[2], 60 to 124 s
checked.result: Correlation 0.952, 0.992 at lag 0.677 s. The output followed the command, so the fault sits at or before the throttle command, not in the ch[2] output stage.
checked.about: A fault in the ch[2] output stage

checked.result: Only two start-up events at 1.264 s (Low voltage warning, Sensor health error). No mode, failsafe or e-stop event later in the flight. No earlier cases apply.
checked.about: Who commanded the throttle to zero

effects.quote: ANOMALY a11 t=113.927 s: actuator.output[ch[1]] changed level for good (1526 -> 1122 us)
effects.why: The pitch-loop surface moved far from trim about 10 s after the throttle cut, a reaction to the unstable attitude.

effects.quote: ANOMALY a12 t=114.148 s: vehicle.altitude[relative] changed level for good (50.145 -> 33.326 m)
effects.why: The descent follows the loss of thrust.

effects.quote: ANOMALY a7 t=110.442 s: vehicle.attitude[pitch] followed control.attitude_setpoint[pitch] worse for good (typical |error| 1.31 -> 16.83)
effects.why: Tracking degraded after thrust was lost.

next_action.why: This recording shows throttle and ch[2] going to zero but not who commanded it. The autopilot log should show a mode or failsafe change, an operator input, or a motor or battery fault.
how: Export the flight controller log (for example a MAVLink or .bag log) for the full flight
Look at mode, failsafe, arming, RC throttle input and battery voltage and current from 95 s to 110 s
Check ESC or motor telemetry and any status text at about 103.3 s
next_action.baseline: Throttle, battery voltage and current earlier in this flight, when throttle was healthy at a median near 46 %.

outcomes.label: Failsafe or mode change at 103.3 s
outcomes.means: The throttle cut was a commanded protection or mode action. Investigate what tripped it, such as the roll excursion or battery.
outcomes.then: Trace the trigger signal that preceded the failsafe

outcomes.label: Operator or RC throttle input went to zero
outcomes.means: The cut was an operator or link action, not a machine fault.
outcomes.then: Close as operator action and check the RC link

outcomes.label: Throttle command stayed high; ESC or RPM dropped
outcomes.means: The recorded 0 is not the real command, and the fault is in the propulsion hardware or path.
outcomes.then: Inspect the ESC, motor and wiring

unknowns: Who or what set the throttle to zero at 103.268 s; the recording has no mode, failsafe or operator event.
Battery voltage and current, ESC and motor data are not in this recording, so a battery or motor fault cannot be ruled out.
Whether the roll excursion shortly before the cut was a cause of it or only a coincident disturbance.

already_answered.question: Did a control fault occur, and when?
already_answered.answer: Yes. Throttle went to zero at 103.268 s and held. Attitude control broke down from about 110 s and fully by 113.6 s.
already_answered.quote: CONSTANT propulsion.throttle was varying, then held 0 from t=103.268 s to the end of the recording (20.916 s, 54 samples)

already_answered.answer: The propulsion loop, through throttle and output channel ch[2]. The control surface channels moved afterwards.

data_requests.what: Autopilot log with mode, failsafe, RC input, battery and ESC telemetry
data_requests.window: Whole flight, focus 95 s to 125 s
data_requests.why_needed: Separates a commanded throttle cut from a propulsion hardware or battery fault.

unobservable.fact: Real motor thrust and ESC state
unobservable.why_it_matters: The recording shows only the commanded output, so a motor or ESC failure cannot be told from a command cut.
unobservable.how_to_observe: Read ESC telemetry from the autopilot log, or bench test the motor and ESC.

hypotheses.claim: The throttle was commanded to zero by the controller, a failsafe or an operator, causing loss of thrust.
hypotheses.because: Throttle held 0 with the ch[2] output obeying it; no event explains it, so the source is unknown.

hypotheses.claim: The motor or ESC failed, and the recorded throttle zero came from a reaction to it.
hypotheses.because: The recording holds only commanded values, so real motor state is not observed. The output followed the command.

hypotheses.claim: Low battery voltage caused a protective throttle cut.
hypotheses.because: A Low voltage warning appears only at start-up (1.264 s). No battery signal is in the data.

hypotheses.claim: The attitude control loop or control surfaces failed independently.
hypotheses.because: Tracking error was small at the throttle cut and rose only about 10 s later; surface channels moved after it.

hypotheses.claim: A bad airspeed sensor triggered the failure.
hypotheses.because: Airspeed is 0 for the whole recording, so it did not change at the cut. It may still affect control quality.

events.what: Throttle drops to 0 and holds from 103.268 s
events.why: Earliest persistent change in the propulsion loop, with no event explaining it.

events.what: ch[2] output falls to 1100 and holds
events.why: It follows the throttle command at about 0.7 s lag.

events.what: Attitude tracking degrades from about 110 s
events.why: It comes after the throttle cut.

events.what: Control surface shifts and altitude loss at 113.6 to 114.1 s
events.why: This is the aircraft's response to the loss of thrust and control.

events.what: Low voltage warning and Sensor health error at 1.264 s
events.why: Start-up warnings, and nothing later points back to them.

events.what: Early level shifts at 7.6 s and 27.2 s
events.why: They look like early manoeuvres, and tracking was normal afterwards.

result.lesson: No earlier cases are in the workspace, so none apply.
result.reuse_when: The same UAV with a similar autopilot recording, where throttle drops to 0 and holds with its output channel obeying and no failsafe event logged. Check the autopilot log for the source of the cut.
